learning: If progress rises and rms_error and steering_oscillation hold, the larger footprint helps the edge reading. If rms_error or oscillation worsens, the footprint is blurring the centring signal, and kp may need a small change or the footprint should return to 0.012. Check the slalom line loss, which was 1 in iteration 3, against the s-bend result.
notes: Baseline body and +/-0.03 m, y=0.04 array from iteration 3, with the Builder's sensor_size test at 0.016. Controller held at iteration 3 values so the sensor footprint is the only change.
rationale: Iteration 3 is the only race on the baseline body with the wider spread, and it scored 52.1 with s-bend progress 0.16 and 1 line-loss event. That isolates the earlier drop to the lighter body. Iteration 2 (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) gave s-bend progress 0.1275, and iteration 3 with the baseline body recovered it to 0.16. The Builder's proposal keeps that body and the +/-0.03 m, y=0.04, 15 mm array, and changes only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016. I accept the geometry unchanged. I also keep the iteration 3 controller exactly (base_speed 1.5, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction), so any change in progress, line loss or rms_error can be attributed to the sensor footprint. The main integration risk is that 16 mm footprints at 15 mm spacing overlap heavily, which flattens the signal near the centre and can raise signal magnitude at the edges. That changes the effective steering gain, so kp is not retuned until the race shows whether rms_error or oscillation moves. Expected result, which is not a measurement: progress at or above 0.16, line loss at or below 1, and a score near or above 52.1. The race will show whether the larger footprint helps the edge reading or blurs the centring signal.
